result.rationale: The migration inserts legacy values verbatim ('INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES (\'#{h}\')') without stripping protocol/path, while EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? matches via `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` against URI(referer).host. The stripping only happens in before_validation on save, and never for migration-inserted rows. So a legacy value like 'http://discourse.org' (a format the deleted SiteSetting specs show was supported) can never match a referer host, breaking embedding after upgrade. This is a real correctness/data-migration defect introduced by this diff.

judged_text: The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim without stripping protocol or path, but EmbeddableHost.record_for_host matches lower(host) = URI(referer).host, so migrated rows like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' — formats the removed specs show the old allows_embeddable_host? explicitly supported — can never match any referer. Sites upgrading with URL-formatted host entries silently lose embedding immediately after the migration: every embedded-comments request raises Discourse::InvalidAccess until an admin hand-fixes each broken row in the new UI.
